title: Geo-interleaved pool placement with soft failover and residency safeguards
creator: Asha Patel
description: Design and implement an interleaved placement strategy for multi-zone/regional dedicated capacity that provides explicit throughput guarantees, predictable autoscaling behavior, and enforceable data residency constraints. The feature must support: (1) capacity reservations that guarantee steady-state throughput per-customer, (2) soft-failover semantics that preserve throughput tiers during zone evacuations, and (3) residency and KMS scoping so customer data/tokenization never leaves the approved residency boundary.
background: Customers buying Dedicated pools require both predictable throughput and strong residency guarantees. Current single-zone reservations have brittle failover and can either over-provision or provide poor tail latency during zone loss. We propose an interleaved placement scheme where reserved capacity for a customer is spread across multiple AZs/edge racks in a weighted fashion, combined with a soft-failover orchestration layer that reallocates traffic without hard rebalancing that would violate residency constraints.
design_decisions: Interleaved shards: each dedicated reservation is split into N shards and placed across zones using a weighted hash to ensure cross-zone throughput diversity and faster failover headroom.
Throughput guarantees expressed as min_qps + burst_tokens: runtime enforces a stable per-reservation baseline and a configurable token-bucket for controlled bursts.

Soft-failover policy: when a zone shows degraded health, route to remaining shards with prioritized lane (latency-sensitive lanes first). Do not automatically move KV cache between zones to preserve residency semantics; instead use per-shard warm standbys and KV-prefetch hints.

Autoscale behavior: two-tier autoscaler with (A) fast vertical scale inside shard (hot scaling within GPU for short spikes) and (B) slow horizontal scale adding whole shards for sustained demand with a cooldown and reconciliation window.
Residency controls: each shard tagged with residency label and encrypted with region-scoped KMS key; control plane enforces that no shard is created outside allowed regions for that reservation.
Rollback/fallback: provide model-variant fallback lanes (quantized smaller models) that are residency-compatible to preserve availability when full model capacity isn't available.
Operator controls: console exposes shard distribution, soft-evacuation thresholds, and an emergency cross-region drain toggle requiring SRE approval and audit log entry.
work_items: Runtime: implement shard placement algorithm and weighted hash placement (ENG-runtime).
Orchestrator: implement soft-failover routing, per-reservation token-buckets, and shard lifecycle APIs.
Autoscaler: multi-timescale controller (fast inner loop + slow shard scaler) with graceful shrink policy.
Security: KMS integration per-region and residency policy enforcement at create-time with unit tests.
Console: new dedicated-pool view showing interleaved placement and failover simulation controls.
Docs & SDK: API fields for reservation_shards, min_qps, burst_tokens, residency_scope and examples.
E2E tests: synthetic traffic across AZ failure injection and KV cache warm-standby verification.
Launch: create migration script to convert existing single-zone reservations to interleaved shards with owner approval.
acceptance_criteria: Create a dedicated reservation with shards=3 across zones eu-west-1a/b/c and verify min_qps is honored on steady-state traffic for each customer account.
Simulate one AZ outage; soft-failover must route traffic to remaining shards within 12s with no customer-visible drop in success rate >1% for P95 latency under 99th percentile SLO target.
Residency assertion tests: attempts to create a shard in non-authorized region are blocked and audited.
Autoscaler: sustained 20% above min_qps for 10 minutes scales horizontal shard count up; scaled-down shards enter soft-shrink with 30-minute grace period before eviction.
Console shows correct shard topology and the failover simulation reproduces routing changes seen in logs.
Security review completed and KMS rotation path documented and tested.
rollout_plan: Stage 1: internal canary with two pilot customers, shards=3, read-only metrics for 2 weeks. Stage 2: enable for small new customers with opt-in migration tool. Stage 3: default for new dedicated reservations and offer assisted migrations for large customers. Each stage gated on SLO telemetry and security sign-off.
metrics: P95 / P99 latency for requests during failover windows
risks_and_mitigations: Increased cross-zone networking cost: mitigate via placement weight tuning and preferring AZ-local shards where residency allows.
KV cache cold-start on failover: use warm-standby prefetch and prioritized cache warming for top-k prefixes.
Complexity in autoscaler interactions: decouple fast inner-loop and slow shard scaler, add chaos tests and staged rollouts.
Residency enforcement bugs: require policy gate in control plane and automated unit tests and operational audits.
Customer confusion around billing changes: include clear documentation and migration cost-estimates in Console.
